claims.text: Bun maintainers publicly said Bun 1.0 was "stable and production-ready," so a production-readiness claim from maintainers is directly evidenced.
Concrete compatibility evidence exists in Bun's published test results: Bun 1.4 said several Node modules passed 97% of Node's tests, `node:quic` passed 99%, and some modules passed 100%.
Bun's own compatibility docs also document remaining gaps, including partial `node:async_hooks`, partial `node:child_process`, and `node:cluster` being implemented but not battle-tested.

For native addons, the evidence is mixed rather than absolute: Bun's tracker says all `napi_*` and `node_api_*` functions were implemented, but the reported combined Node-API status was 74 pass / 23 todo / 76.3% on Linux.

Users and platform operators report some successful production use: one discussion participant said they had used Bun in production since April 2023 on Heroku, and Vercel launched Bun runtime support in public beta while recommending Node.js for maximum compatibility.
acceptable_patterns: used it in production since April 2023

claims.text: Users also report concrete production problems, including memory growth or crashes, production-mode-only failures, and `bun install --production` problems; Bun later said one workspace `--production` devDependency bug was fixed.
acceptable_patterns: worked in development mode but failed in production mode
lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen
this is no longer the case

rejected_claims.text: Bun is universally production-safe for Node.js workloads.
rejected_claims.reason: Overly broad; the supplied evidence shows documented gaps and multiple production bug reports.

rejected_claims.text: Virtually any Node.js app works on Bun.
rejected_claims.reason: This is a maintainer marketing claim in the supplied evidence, but not independently established by the cited compatibility and issue evidence.

rejected_claims.text: Bun is broadly unreliable in production.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported as a general statement; the evidence proves specific failures existed, not prevalence across all production users.

rejected_claims.text: AsyncLocalStorage performance on Bun blocks production OpenTelemetry.
rejected_claims.reason: Time-unstable/contradictory in the supplied evidence because the cited issue was later updated to say the reported production problem did not exist in release builds.
